topic_tag: a harvest procession over fifty years
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Writing in 1990, one folklorist concluded that the changes of the previous fifty years had ______ the custom.

worlds.passage: For centuries the villages of one mountain valley marked the end of the olive harvest with a night procession, led by singers, from the church to the presses. Until the 1940s only the men of six landowning families could carry the lanterns or sing the verses, a right passed from father to son. As those families sold their groves and moved to the coast, the village councils stopped asking whose son a singer was, and by the 1980s most of those who carried the lanterns were hired pickers and their daughters. Writing in 1990, one folklorist concluded that the changes of the previous fifty years had ______ the custom.
worlds.explanation: Roles once inherited by six families' sons stopped being checked for lineage, and hired pickers and their daughters came to fill them, so the changes had "democratized" the custom. "Dramatized" fails because nothing turned the procession into a show for an audience; only who took part changed. "Enshrined" fails because no law or formal honor fixed it in place; the councils loosened its rules. "Harmonized" fails because the change concerned who performed, not differences among the villages' versions.

dramatized.quote: stopped asking whose son a singer was
dramatized.why: the change was in who could take part, not in staging the event for spectators

enshrined.why: the councils relaxed the custom's rules rather than fixing it as a protected tradition

harmonized.why: what changed was the singers' social origin, not separate village versions being brought into line

worlds.passage: For centuries the villages of one mountain valley marked the end of the olive harvest with a night procession, led by singers, from the church to the presses. After a road reached the valley in the 1950s, buses brought visitors each November, and the villages moved the procession from midnight to early evening. Singers began rehearsing for weeks in costumes copied from old photographs, and a narrator explained each verse over loudspeakers to visitors seated along the route, while the same six families who had always led it went on leading it. Writing in 1990, one folklorist concluded that the changes of the previous fifty years had ______ the custom.
worlds.explanation: The procession was retimed, costumed, rehearsed, and narrated over loudspeakers to seated visitors, so it had been "dramatized," turned into a staged performance. "Democratized" fails because the visitors only watched and the same six families still led it. "Enshrined" fails because the changes reshaped the event for spectators instead of fixing it as it was. "Harmonized" fails because nothing brought differing village versions into agreement.

democratized.quote: the same six families who had always led it
democratized.why: leadership stayed in the same families and visitors were seated spectators, so participation was not opened up

enshrined.quote: moved the procession from midnight to early evening
enshrined.why: the custom was altered for an audience, not preserved and protected unchanged

harmonized.why: the changes add staging and spectacle; none reconciles different village versions

worlds.passage: For centuries the villages of one mountain valley marked the end of the olive harvest with a night procession, led by singers, from the church to the presses. In 1951 a national law added the procession to a list of forty "living monuments" of the country. From then on the state closed the route to traffic on each harvest night, paid to repair the presses and lanterns, and sent an inspector every year to confirm that route, verses, and singers matched the description filed in 1951, while neighboring valleys' customs lapsed. Writing in 1990, one folklorist concluded that the changes of the previous fifty years had ______ the custom.
worlds.explanation: A national law listed the procession as a monument, the state funded its upkeep, and an inspector held it each year to its 1951 form, so the changes had "enshrined" the custom, preserving it as something honored and protected. "Democratized" fails because the singers had to match the 1951 description, so participation was not opened up. "Dramatized" fails because the event was held to its old form, not restaged as a show. "Harmonized" fails because each village's procession was kept as described rather than made uniform.

democratized.quote: singers matched the description filed in 1951
democratized.why: the singers were held to their recorded form, so participation was not widened

dramatized.quote: sent an inspector every year to confirm
dramatized.why: the state checked that the event stayed as it was, which rules out reshaping it into a show

harmonized.why: each procession was preserved against its own record, not brought into line with the others

worlds.passage: For centuries the villages of one mountain valley marked the end of the olive harvest with a night procession, led by singers, from the church to the presses. Before 1940 each village sang its own verses to its own tune, and singers from neighboring villages could barely follow one another. From 1950 a regional radio station broadcast one village's procession every harvest night, and a folklorist recording the processions in 1985 found that singers from any of the nine villages could join any other village's procession without a rehearsal. Writing in 1990, one folklorist concluded that the changes of the previous fifty years had ______ the custom.
worlds.explanation: Singers who once could barely follow a neighboring village could, after decades of hearing one broadcast version, join any village's procession unrehearsed, so the changes had "harmonized" the custom, bringing its versions into agreement. "Democratized" fails because nothing changed about who was allowed to sing. "Dramatized" fails because the processions were not restaged for spectators. "Enshrined" fails because the convergence happened informally through listening, with no law or formal honor.

democratized.why: the change concerns whether villages' versions matched, not who was permitted to sing

dramatized.quote: join any other village's procession without a rehearsal
dramatized.why: the evidence is that the versions now matched, not that the event was staged for an audience

enshrined.why: the shared version spread informally by listening, not by any formal act preserving the custom
